intro: Hi! You can already say how long something has been true with the present perfect (I've lived here since 2020). Now you'll talk about activities that are still going on (I've been waiting for an hour!), explain what people can see (I'm tired because I've been running), and choose between I've read and I've been reading. Warm-up: what have you been doing today?
teachingNotes: This lesson builds on b1-present-perfect: have/has + third form, for (a length of time) / since (a starting point), How long…?, and present perfect vs past simple are known. Recap them in one line only. New here: have/has + been + -ing form (the present perfect continuous) for an activity that started in the past and is still going on. Stress that 's = has in she's/he's/it's been, and that been is just the third form of be (already known); -ing spelling is as in the present continuous (running, making, studying).

Duration: the Indonesian trap is 'Saya sudah menunggu dari tadi' / 'Saya sedang menunggu di sini sejak jam 7' → the node's error *'I am waiting here for an hour' → 'I've been waiting here for an hour'. Always say why: the present continuous is only about now and can't take for/since/How long. Questions: How long have/has + subject + been + -ing? (*'How long are you waiting?'). Time words: for, since, all morning / all day (sepanjang pagi / seharian). 'I've waited for an hour' is also correct English: accept it, but teach the continuous for an activity that is still going on. With live, work, study and teach + for/since both forms are fine (I've lived / I've been living here for ten years): never make those either-or, never mark one wrong.

Recent activity with a visible result: the activity has just stopped and you can see the result now (I'm tired because I've been running; Your eyes are red. Have you been crying?; The streets are wet. It's been raining.). Indonesian 'habis lari' (= baru selesai lari) leads to *'I'm tired because I'm running' (you aren't running now) or *'because I just run'. A past simple like 'I ran 5 km this morning' is fine for telling a finished event; accept it in free answers, but tasks that ask for the present perfect continuous expect have/has been + -ing.

Simple vs continuous: simple = the result, how many / how much, finished (I've read three books; I've painted the kitchen = it's done). Continuous = the activity, how long, maybe not finished (I've been reading all morning; I've been painting the kitchen = that's why there's paint on my shirt). The node's error *'I've been reading three books this month' → 'I've read three books this month': a number of things done → simple (this month = bulan ini, still going on; gloss it, don't teach unfinished-time words). Test only clear cases: a number of things done → simple; state verb → simple; visible result of an activity / still going on → continuous.

State verbs (feelings, thoughts, owning: know, like, love, believe, understand, have = own, be) stay in the simple form even for how long: the node's error *'I've been knowing her for years' → 'I've known her for years'. Explain the exception that looks like it breaks the rule: have breakfast / a meeting / a shower is an activity, so 'We've been having a meeting all morning' is fine. Don't test want, love or think in the continuous (native speakers do say 'I've been wanting…', 'I've been thinking…'); test know, have (own), believe, understand.

Limits: no past perfect (continuous), passive, reported speech, second conditional, relative clauses or used to. Don't teach recently/lately, unfinished-time words (this week, today, so far) or the 'temporary situation' nuance as rules; if the learner uses them correctly, accept them. Keep sentences natural for B1 (work, campus, home, Indonesian contexts) and explanations in plain Indonesian with 'kamu'.

keyPoints.title: have/has been + -ing: how long
keyPoints.explanation: For an activity that started in the past and is still going on now, use have/has + been + -ing: I've been waiting for an hour (and I'm still waiting). Not 'I am waiting here for an hour': the present continuous is only about now and can't take for or since. she's/he's been = she/he has been. Ask: How long have you been + -ing? Answer: For two years. / Since 2024.

examples.en: I've been waiting for the bus for forty minutes.
examples.id: Saya sudah empat puluh menit menunggu bus.

examples.en: Rina has been working since 7 o'clock.
How long have you been learning English? — For two years.
examples.id: Sudah berapa lama kamu belajar bahasa Inggris? — Sudah dua tahun.

id.title: have/has been + -ing: sudah berapa lama
id.explanation: Untuk kegiatan yang dimulai di masa lalu dan masih berlangsung sekarang, pakai have/has + been + -ing: I've been waiting for an hour (dan saya masih menunggu). Bukan 'I am waiting here for an hour': present continuous hanya tentang sekarang dan tidak bisa dipakai dengan for atau since. she's/he's been = she/he has been. Bertanya: How long have you been + -ing? Jawab: For two years. / Since 2024.

keyPoints.title: Visible results of a recent activity
keyPoints.explanation: When an activity has just stopped and you can see the result now (tired, wet, dirty, red eyes), use have/has been + -ing to explain it: I'm tired because I've been running. Ask about what you see: Your eyes are red. Have you been crying? Indonesian 'habis lari' is not 'I'm running' (you aren't running now): it's I've been running.

examples.en: I'm tired because I've been running.
Your eyes are red. Have you been crying?
Your hands are dirty! Have you been working in the garden?

id.title: Hasil yang terlihat dari kegiatan yang baru selesai
id.explanation: Kalau sebuah kegiatan baru saja berhenti dan hasilnya terlihat sekarang (capek, basah, kotor, mata merah), pakai have/has been + -ing untuk menjelaskannya: I'm tired because I've been running. Tanyakan apa yang kamu lihat: Your eyes are red. Have you been crying? 'Habis lari' bukan 'I'm running' (kamu tidak sedang lari sekarang), tapi I've been running.

keyPoints.title: I've read or I've been reading?
keyPoints.explanation: Present perfect simple (have/has + third form) = the result: how many, finished. I've read three books (not 'I've been reading three books'). Present perfect continuous (have/has been + -ing) = the activity: how long, maybe not finished. I've been reading all morning. State verbs (know, like, believe, understand, have = own, be) stay simple: I've known her for years (not 'I've been knowing her'). With live, work and study + for/since, both are fine.

examples.en: I've read three books this month. / I've been reading all morning.
examples.id: Bulan ini saya sudah membaca tiga buku. / Dari pagi saya membaca.

examples.en: I've lived here for ten years. = I've been living here for ten years.
examples.id: Saya sudah sepuluh tahun tinggal di sini.

id.title: I've read atau I've been reading?
id.explanation: Present perfect simple (have/has + bentuk ketiga) = hasilnya: berapa banyak, sudah selesai. I've read three books (bukan 'I've been reading three books'). Present perfect continuous (have/has been + -ing) = kegiatannya: berapa lama, mungkin belum selesai. I've been reading all morning. Kata kerja keadaan (know, like, believe, understand, have = punya, be) tetap simple: I've known her for years (bukan 'I've been knowing her'). Dengan live, work dan study + for/since, dua-duanya benar.

guidedPractice.prompt: Present perfect simple or continuous of 'write'? I ___ ten emails since lunch.

assessment.prompt: Complete with the present perfect continuous of 'try': I ___ to call Budi since lunch, but he isn't answering his phone.
acceptableAnswers: have been trying
've been trying
assessment.rubric: Correct: have been trying / 've been trying (started at lunch, still going on). 'am trying' = 20 (the Indonesian 'sedang' trap: the present continuous can't take since). 'have tried' = 60 (correct English, but the task asks for the continuous). 'has been trying' = 60 (I → have). 'have been try' = 40. 'was trying' = 10.

assessment.prompt: Correct the mistake: Bu Ani is teaching at this school for fifteen years.
acceptableAnswers: bu ani has been teaching at this school for fifteen years
bu ani has been teaching at this school for 15 years
bu ani's been teaching at this school for fifteen years
bu ani's been teaching at this school for 15 years
bu ani has taught at this school for fifteen years
bu ani has taught at this school for 15 years

bu ani's taught at this school for 15 years
assessment.rubric: Correct: Bu Ani has been teaching (or has taught) at this school for fifteen years: with teach + for, both forms are right. 'Bu Ani teaches at this school for fifteen years' = 20 (still the Indonesian trap: present + for). 'Bu Ani has been teaching … since fifteen years' = 50 (fifteen years is a length → for). 'Bu Ani have been teaching' = 60 (Bu Ani = she → has). 'Bu Ani has been teach' = 40. Sentence unchanged = 0.

assessment.prompt: Write a question with 'How long' and the present perfect continuous (Sudah berapa lama kamu mengerjakan laporan ini?): you / work / on this report
acceptableAnswers: how long have you been working on this report
assessment.rubric: Correct: How long have you been working on this report? 'How long have you worked on this report?' = 70 (correct English, but the task asks for the continuous). 'How long are you working on this report?' = 20 (the Indonesian trap: present continuous). 'How long you have been working on this report?' = 60 (statement word order). 'How long have you been work' = 40. 'How long did you work' = 10 (finished time; the work is still going on).

assessment.prompt: Your friend comes back from the parking area. Her hands are black with oil. Ask her a question with the present perfect continuous: you / fix / your motorbike
acceptableAnswers: have you been fixing your motorbike
have you been fixing your motorcycle
have you been fixing your bike
assessment.rubric: Correct: Have you been fixing your motorbike? (asking about the activity that explains the dirty hands). 'Are you fixing your motorbike?' = 20 (she isn't fixing it now). 'Did you fix your motorbike?' = 50 (correct English, but it asks about a finished event, not the activity behind the result; the task asks for the present perfect continuous). 'Have you fixed your motorbike?' = 50 (asks about the result: is it working now?). 'You have been fixing your motorbike?' = 60 (statement word order). 'Have you been fix' = 40.

assessment.prompt: Say it in English with the present perfect continuous. Start with 'I'm tired because…': Saya capek, habis main futsal.
acceptableAnswers: i'm tired because i've been playing futsal
i am tired because i have been playing futsal
i'm tired because i have been playing futsal
i am tired because i've been playing futsal
assessment.rubric: Correct: I'm tired because I've been playing futsal (the playing has just stopped; the tiredness is the visible result). 'I'm tired because I played futsal' = 60 (correct English for a finished event, but the task asks for the present perfect continuous). 'I'm tired because I'm playing futsal' = 20 (not playing now; the 'habis' trap). 'because I just play futsal' = 10. 'because I've been play futsal' = 40. 'because I've played futsal' = 50.

assessment.prompt: Put the verb in the right form (present perfect simple or continuous): Pak Budi's stall is very busy today. He ___ (sell) 40 cups of es teh since 7 a.m.
acceptableAnswers: has sold
's sold
assessment.rubric: Correct: has sold (40 cups = how many → the result → present perfect simple; sell → sold → sold). 'has been selling' = 30 (the node's error: a number of things done takes the simple). 'have sold' = 60 (he → has). 'has sell' / 'has selled' = 40. 'sold' = 30 (since needs the present perfect). 'is selling' = 10.

assessment.prompt: Put the verb in the right form (present perfect simple or continuous): We ___ (have) this car for twelve years. It's old, but it still runs well.
acceptableAnswers: have had
've had
assessment.rubric: Correct: have had (have = punya/own is a state verb → present perfect simple, even for how long). 'have been having' = 30 (the node's error: state verbs don't take -ing). 'have' = 20 (the Indonesian trap: present + for). 'has had' = 60 (we → have). 'had' = 30 (they still have the car).

material.title: Still going on: I've been waiting for an hour

blocks.text:
**Quick recap:** you already use the present perfect, **have/has + third form**, to say how long something has been true: *I've lived here since 2020. How long have you known Sari?* (**for** + a length of time, **since** + a starting point).

Now a new form for an **activity** (kegiatan, something you do) that **started in the past and is still going on now**: **have/has + been + -ing form** (-ing form = verb + -ing, like in *I'm working*). Its name is the **present perfect continuous**.
- *I've been waiting for an hour.* = I started waiting an hour ago, and I'm **still** waiting.
- *Rina has been working since 7 o'clock.* = she started at 7, and she's **still** working.

**Why been + -ing?** Two forms you know, joined together: *I'm waiting* (now) + *I've been here for an hour* (from the past up to now) → **I've been waiting for an hour**. **been** is the third form of *be*; the **-ing** says the activity is still happening.

**Short forms:** I've / you've / we've / they've been… · he's / she's / it's been… (here **'s = has**, not is: *She's been working* = She has been working). The -ing spelling is the same as in the present continuous: *run → running, make → making, study → studying*.

id.text:
**Ulasan singkat:** kamu sudah memakai present perfect, **have/has + bentuk ketiga**, untuk mengatakan sudah berapa lama sesuatu benar: *I've lived here since 2020. How long have you known Sari?* (**for** + lamanya waktu, **since** + titik mulai).

Sekarang ada bentuk baru untuk **kegiatan** (sesuatu yang kamu lakukan) yang **dimulai di masa lalu dan masih berlangsung sekarang**: **have/has + been + bentuk -ing** (bentuk -ing = kata kerja + -ing, seperti di *I'm working*). Namanya **present perfect continuous**.
- *I've been waiting for an hour.* = Saya mulai menunggu satu jam lalu, dan saya **masih** menunggu.
- *Rina has been working since 7 o'clock.* = dia mulai jam 7, dan dia **masih** bekerja.

**Kenapa been + -ing?** Dua bentuk yang sudah kamu kenal, digabung: *I'm waiting* (sekarang) + *I've been here for an hour* (dari masa lalu sampai sekarang) → **I've been waiting for an hour**. **been** adalah bentuk ketiga dari *be*; **-ing** menunjukkan kegiatannya masih berlangsung.

**Bentuk singkat:** I've / you've / we've / they've been… · he's / she's / it's been… (di sini **'s = has**, bukan is: *She's been working* = She has been working). Ejaan -ing sama seperti di present continuous: *run → running, make → making, study → studying*.

blocks.text: **The Indonesian trap:** *Saya sudah menunggu dari tadi* or *Saya sedang menunggu di sini sejak jam 7* has *sedang*, so learners say 'I am waiting here for an hour'. That's wrong: *I'm waiting* only talks about **now**, so it can't take **for an hour** or **since 7**. As soon as you say how long (for, since, How long…?, all morning), use **have/has been + -ing**: *I've been waiting here for an hour.* (You may also hear *I've waited for an hour*: that's correct too, but for an activity that's still going on, people usually choose the -ing form.)

id.text: **Jebakan bahasa Indonesia:** *Saya sudah menunggu dari tadi* atau *Saya sedang menunggu di sini sejak jam 7* memakai *sedang*, jadi pelajar sering bilang 'I am waiting here for an hour'. Itu salah: *I'm waiting* hanya bicara tentang **sekarang**, jadi tidak bisa dipakai dengan **for an hour** atau **since 7**. Begitu kamu mengatakan berapa lama (for, since, How long…?, all morning), pakai **have/has been + -ing**: *I've been waiting here for an hour.* (Kamu mungkin juga mendengar *I've waited for an hour*: itu juga benar, tapi untuk kegiatan yang masih berlangsung, orang biasanya memilih bentuk -ing.)

blocks.prompt: Sari is still at her desk. Complete: She ___ on the new website since 9 a.m.
blocks.explain: She started at 9 a.m. and is still working, and since 9 a.m. says how long → has been working. 'is working' is only about now and can't take since (the 'sedang' trap). 'worked' is for a finished time.

id.prompt: Sari masih di mejanya. Lengkapi: She ___ on the new website since 9 a.m.
id.explain: Dia mulai jam 9 pagi dan masih bekerja, dan since 9 a.m. mengatakan sudah berapa lama → has been working. 'is working' hanya tentang sekarang dan tidak bisa dipakai dengan since (jebakan 'sedang'). 'worked' untuk waktu yang sudah selesai.

id.title: Masih berlangsung: I've been waiting for an hour

blocks.text:
**Questions with How long:** How long + have/has + subject + been + -ing? (subject = who does it: you, she, Pak Hasan). *How long have you been learning English?* — *For two years.* / *Since 2023.* Not 'How long are you learning English?' (the same *sedang* trap).

**Yes/no questions:** Have/Has + subject + been + -ing? *Has Budi been working late?* — *Yes, he has.* / *No, he hasn't.*

**Negative:** haven't / hasn't been + -ing: *I haven't been sleeping well since I moved to Jakarta.*

**Time words:** **for** + a length (*for twenty minutes, for a long time*), **since** + a starting point (*since 8 o'clock, since I arrived*), **all morning / all day / all week** (sepanjang pagi / seharian / sepanjang minggu).

id.text:
**Pertanyaan dengan How long:** How long + have/has + subjek + been + -ing? (subjek = siapa yang melakukan: you, she, Pak Hasan). *How long have you been learning English?* — *For two years.* / *Since 2023.* Bukan 'How long are you learning English?' (jebakan *sedang* yang sama).

**Pertanyaan ya/tidak:** Have/Has + subjek + been + -ing? *Has Budi been working late?* — *Yes, he has.* / *No, he hasn't.*

**Kalimat negatif:** haven't / hasn't been + -ing: *I haven't been sleeping well since I moved to Jakarta.*

**Keterangan waktu:** **for** + lamanya waktu (*for twenty minutes, for a long time*), **since** + titik mulai (*since 8 o'clock, since I arrived*), **all morning / all day / all week** (sepanjang pagi / seharian / sepanjang minggu).

blocks.text: Watch the **'s**: *She's been working* = She **has** been working (dari tadi bekerja). *She's working* = She **is** working (sedang bekerja sekarang). If **been** comes next, 's is **has**.

id.text: Perhatikan **'s**: *She's been working* = She **has** been working (dari tadi bekerja). *She's working* = She **is** working (sedang bekerja sekarang). Kalau sesudahnya ada **been**, 's artinya **has**.

blocks.prompt: Which question means 'Sudah berapa lama kamu belajar menyetir?'
options: How long are you learning to drive?
How long have you been learning to drive?
How long have you learning to drive?
blocks.explain: You started in the past and you're still learning → How long + have + you + been + -ing. 'are you learning' is only about now (the 'sedang' trap), and 'have you learning' is missing been.

id.prompt: Pertanyaan mana yang artinya 'Sudah berapa lama kamu belajar menyetir?'
id.explain: Kamu mulai di masa lalu dan masih belajar → How long + have + you + been + -ing. 'are you learning' hanya tentang sekarang (jebakan 'sedang'), dan 'have you learning' tidak punya been.

material.title: You look tired! Results you can see

blocks.text:
The present perfect continuous also explains **what you can see now**. The activity **has just stopped**, and you can **see the result**: someone is tired, hot, wet or dirty, their eyes are red, the kitchen smells of food.
- *I'm tired because I've been running.* (I stopped a minute ago; the tiredness is the result.)
- *Your eyes are red. Have you been crying?*
- *Your hands are dirty! Have you been working in the garden?*

**The Indonesian trap:** we say *Capek, habis lari* (habis = baru selesai). Learners translate it as 'I'm tired because I'm running' or 'because I just run'. But you aren't running **now**, and 'I just run' isn't the right form. Say **I've been running**: the activity is over, but its result is here now.

The past simple *I ran 5 km this morning* is also correct when you tell a finished event. To **explain what someone can see**, English usually chooses **have/has been + -ing**.

id.text:
Present perfect continuous juga menjelaskan **apa yang terlihat sekarang**. Kegiatannya **baru saja berhenti**, dan kamu bisa **melihat hasilnya**: seseorang capek, kepanasan, basah atau kotor, matanya merah, dapurnya bau masakan.
- *I'm tired because I've been running.* (Saya berhenti semenit lalu; capeknya adalah hasilnya.)
- *Your eyes are red. Have you been crying?*
- *Your hands are dirty! Have you been working in the garden?*

**Jebakan bahasa Indonesia:** kita bilang *Capek, habis lari* (habis = baru selesai). Pelajar sering menerjemahkannya 'I'm tired because I'm running' atau 'because I just run'. Padahal kamu tidak sedang lari **sekarang**, dan 'I just run' bukan bentuk yang benar. Katakan **I've been running**: kegiatannya sudah selesai, tapi hasilnya ada sekarang.

Past simple *I ran 5 km this morning* juga benar kalau kamu menceritakan kejadian yang sudah selesai. Untuk **menjelaskan apa yang dilihat orang**, bahasa Inggris biasanya memilih **have/has been + -ing**.

rows.id: Saya capek karena habis lari.

rows.en: Your eyes are red. Have you been crying?
rows.id: Matamu merah. Kamu habis menangis?

rows.en: The kitchen smells great. Have you been cooking?
rows.id: Dapurnya wangi sekali. Kamu habis masak?

rows.en: Why is the floor wet? — The kids have been playing with water.

blocks.text: See a result → ask about the activity with **Have you been + -ing?** *You're all sweaty! Have you been playing badminton?* Not 'Are you playing badminton?': that asks about **now**, and the person has stopped.

id.text: Lihat hasilnya → tanyakan kegiatannya dengan **Have you been + -ing?** *You're all sweaty! Have you been playing badminton?* Bukan 'Are you playing badminton?': itu bertanya tentang **sekarang**, padahal orangnya sudah berhenti.

material.title: I've read or I've been reading?

blocks.text:
Both forms join the past and now. The difference is what you talk about:
- **present perfect simple** (have/has + third form) = the **result**: **how many / how much**, something **finished**. *I've read three books. I've painted the kitchen* (it's done, come and see).
- **present perfect continuous** (have/has been + -ing) = the **activity**: **how long**, maybe **not finished**. *I've been reading all morning. I've been painting the kitchen* (that's why there's paint on my shirt; maybe it isn't finished).

**A number of things done → simple.** Not 'I've been reading three books this month' but **I've read three books this month** (this month = bulan ini). When you count what's done, you talk about the result.

**Sometimes both are right.** With **live, work, study, teach** + for/since, both forms are fine and mean almost the same: *I've lived here for ten years* = *I've been living here for ten years*. Don't worry about choosing there.

id.text:
Dua bentuk ini sama-sama menyambungkan masa lalu dan sekarang. Bedanya ada pada apa yang kamu bicarakan:
- **present perfect simple** (have/has + bentuk ketiga) = **hasilnya**: **berapa banyak**, sesuatu yang **sudah selesai**. *I've read three books. I've painted the kitchen* (sudah selesai, ayo lihat).
- **present perfect continuous** (have/has been + -ing) = **kegiatannya**: **berapa lama**, mungkin **belum selesai**. *I've been reading all morning. I've been painting the kitchen* (makanya ada cat di bajuku; mungkin belum selesai).

**Jumlah hal yang sudah selesai → simple.** Bukan 'I've been reading three books this month', tapi **I've read three books this month** (this month = bulan ini). Kalau kamu menghitung apa yang sudah selesai, kamu bicara tentang hasilnya.

**Kadang dua-duanya benar.** Dengan **live, work, study, teach** + for/since, dua bentuk ini sama-sama benar dan artinya hampir sama: *I've lived here for ten years* = *I've been living here for ten years*. Di sini kamu tidak perlu pusing memilih.

blocks.prompt: Complete: Sari ___ five job applications since Monday.
blocks.explain: five applications = how many → the result → present perfect simple: has sent. 'has been sending' talks about the activity, not a number of things done. 'is sending' is only about now and can't take since.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: Sari ___ five job applications since Monday.
id.explain: five applications = berapa banyak → hasilnya → present perfect simple: has sent. 'has been sending' bicara tentang kegiatannya, bukan jumlah yang sudah selesai. 'is sending' hanya tentang sekarang dan tidak bisa dipakai dengan since.

id.title: I've read atau I've been reading?

material.title: State verbs: I've known her for years

blocks.text:
Some verbs are not activities but **states** (keadaan): feelings, thoughts and owning. They **don't take -ing**, so they stay in the **present perfect simple**, even when you say how long:
- **know** (tahu, kenal), **like**, **love**, **believe** (percaya), **understand** (mengerti), **have** (= punya), **be**.

Not 'I've been knowing her for years' but **I've known her for years**. Not 'We've been having this house since 2010' but **We've had this house since 2010**.

**be** is already fine: *I've been here since 8 o'clock* is the simple form (**been** is the third form of *be*), so there's no 'been being'.

**Why is 'We've been having a meeting' right?** **have** = punya is a state, but *have a meeting, have lunch, have a shower* are **activities** (things you do), so they can take -ing: *We've been having a meeting all morning.*

id.text:
Beberapa kata kerja bukan kegiatan, tapi **keadaan**: perasaan, pikiran dan kepemilikan. Kata kerja ini **tidak memakai -ing**, jadi tetap dalam **present perfect simple**, walaupun kamu mengatakan berapa lama:
- **know** (tahu, kenal), **like** (suka), **love** (cinta, sangat suka), **believe** (percaya), **understand** (mengerti), **have** (= punya), **be**.

Bukan 'I've been knowing her for years', tapi **I've known her for years**. Bukan 'We've been having this house since 2010', tapi **We've had this house since 2010**.

**be** sudah benar: *I've been here since 8 o'clock* adalah bentuk simple (**been** adalah bentuk ketiga dari *be*), jadi tidak ada 'been being'.

**Kenapa 'We've been having a meeting' benar?** **have** = punya adalah keadaan, tapi *have a meeting, have lunch, have a shower* adalah **kegiatan** (sesuatu yang kamu lakukan), jadi boleh memakai -ing: *We've been having a meeting all morning.*

rows.en: I've known Budi for years.
rows.id: Saya sudah bertahun-tahun kenal Budi.

rows.en: My parents have had their warung for twenty years.
rows.id: Orang tua saya sudah dua puluh tahun punya warung.

rows.en: I've always liked durian.
rows.id: Dari dulu saya suka durian.

rows.en: We've been having a meeting all morning.
rows.id: Kami rapat sepanjang pagi.
rows.note: have a meeting = an activity → -ing is fine

options: I've been knowing Pak Hasan since I was a child.
I know Pak Hasan since I was a child.
I've known Pak Hasan since I was a child.
blocks.explain: know is a state verb, so it stays in the present perfect simple, even with since: I've known. 'I've been knowing' adds -ing to a state verb, and 'I know … since' is the Indonesian trap (present + since).

id.explain: know adalah kata kerja keadaan, jadi tetap present perfect simple, walaupun ada since: I've known. 'I've been knowing' memberi -ing pada kata kerja keadaan, dan 'I know … since' adalah jebakan bahasa Indonesia (present + since).

resources.title: How to use the present perfect continuous tense - 6 Minute Grammar
resources.note: A six-minute episode on the present perfect continuous: activities that are still going on or have just finished, with for and since, and a short quiz. It also mentions recently and lately, which this lesson doesn't cover. The presenters speak at natural speed: turn on the subtitles.

id.note: Episode enam menit tentang present perfect continuous: kegiatan yang masih berlangsung atau baru selesai, dengan for dan since, dan kuis singkat. Video ini juga menyebut recently dan lately, yang tidak dibahas di pelajaran ini. Pembawa acaranya berbicara dengan kecepatan normal: nyalakan subtitelnya.

resources.title: Present perfect simple and continuous
resources.note: A B1–B2 page on choosing between the simple and the continuous (result or activity, how many or how long, visible results), with two practice tests. It also says the continuous can show that a situation is temporary, which this lesson doesn't test.

id.note: Halaman level B1–B2 tentang memilih antara simple dan continuous (hasil atau kegiatan, berapa banyak atau berapa lama, hasil yang terlihat), dengan dua tes latihan. Halaman ini juga menjelaskan bahwa continuous bisa menunjukkan situasi yang sementara, yang tidak diujikan di pelajaran ini.

id.intro: Hai! Kamu sudah bisa mengatakan sudah berapa lama sesuatu benar dengan present perfect (I've lived here since 2020). Sekarang kamu belajar bicara tentang kegiatan yang masih berlangsung (I've been waiting for an hour!), menjelaskan apa yang terlihat (I'm tired because I've been running), dan memilih antara I've read dan I've been reading. Pemanasan: what have you been doing today? (Hari ini kamu ngapain aja?)
suggestedQuestions: Kenapa 'I've been waiting for an hour', bukan 'I am waiting for an hour'?
Apa bedanya 'I've read' dan 'I've been reading'?
Kenapa saya tidak boleh bilang 'I've been knowing her'?
Apakah 'I've lived here for ten years' berbeda dengan 'I've been living here for ten years'?

assessment.ppc-1: Lengkapi dengan present perfect continuous dari 'try': I ___ to call Budi since lunch, but he isn't answering his phone.
assessment.ppc-2: Perbaiki kesalahannya: Bu Ani is teaching at this school for fifteen years.
assessment.ppc-3: Tulis pertanyaan dalam bahasa Inggris dengan 'How long' dan present perfect continuous (Sudah berapa lama kamu mengerjakan laporan ini?): you / work / on this report
assessment.ppc-4: Temanmu kembali dari tempat parkir. Tangannya hitam kena oli. Tanyakan dalam bahasa Inggris dengan present perfect continuous: you / fix / your motorbike
assessment.ppc-5: Katakan dalam bahasa Inggris dengan present perfect continuous. Mulai dengan 'I'm tired because…': Saya capek, habis main futsal.
assessment.ppc-6: Tulis kata kerjanya dalam bentuk yang benar (present perfect simple atau continuous): Pak Budi's stall is very busy today. He ___ (sell) 40 cups of es teh since 7 a.m.
assessment.ppc-7: Tulis kata kerjanya dalam bentuk yang benar (present perfect simple atau continuous): We ___ (have) this car for twelve years. It's old, but it still runs well.
